newsitem.title: UK: Chesterton drops as chief executive quits.
newsitem.headline: Chesterton drops as chief executive quits.

text.p: Chesterton International Plc shares dropped on Friday as the property consultancy said its chief executive was standing down and posted a sharp drop in yearly profits after heavy one-off charges.
Chairman William Wells said the results were highly disappointing and the company had taken a number of "rigorous measures" to address the problems.

He said chief executive Giles Ballantine had agreed to stand down with immediate effect after six years in the post. The company had instructed a firm of accountants to undertake a review of internal financial controls.

Wells said the fall in profits reflected one-off accounting write-offs uncovered in a recently-completed audit as well as investment costs. Gavin Black, chairman of the company's UK business, stood in as acting chief executive, he said.
The stock was down 33-1/2p at 70 by 0956 GMT.
Chesterton's pre-tax profit dropped to 2.4 million stg from 5.3 million a year before on turnover which rose to 89.7 million stg from 69.3 million. The total dividend was held at 3.0p.
Wells said current trading and order levels were strong and the property market had picked up, underpinning the company's confidence in prospects for the current year.
